candidates.title: Massano, Konstantin Sibold, SOEL
candidates.summary: Massano brings his Simulate party to Knockdown Center's Main Hall with Konstantin Sibold and SOEL, Friday Oct 23, 10pm, 21+. Dice lists the all-in price at $43.32 and StubHub flags it as nearly sold out. Big industrial room in Maspeth, proper sound.
candidates.fit: This is the melodic/progressive techno lane he actually lives in - Massano is the Afterlife/Anjuna-adjacent end of the spectrum, closer to Rebuke and Tinlicker than to any bro-club booking. Friday night, warehouse, no table minimums.

candidates.title: Ahmed Spins, Sapian, Mehdi
candidates.summary: Zimbabwean-born, Johannesburg-raised DJ Ahmed Spins headlines Knockdown Center on Saturday Oct 24, 11pm to 3am, with Sapian and Mehdi. Dice lists tickets from $38.17. This is the Afro-house end of the South African scene rather than a commercial Afrobeats club night.
candidates.fit: His current phase is Afrobeats, amapiano and Afro-house, and this is that music in a real warehouse with a sound system instead of a Midtown lounge with bottle service. Pairs with the Massano night if the guys want a two-night weekend.

candidates.title: Mister Sunday: Floating Points and Justin Carter
candidates.time_text: 3pm to 9pm; Justin Carter 3-6, Floating Points 6-8, b2b 8-9
candidates.summary: Mister Sunday is Nowadays' long-running outdoor Sunday party in the backyard, 3pm to 9pm, and this is the penultimate one of the season. Floating Points joins resident Justin Carter, with a b2b for the last hour. RA lists the full set times; ticket price was not visible on the pages I could read.
candidates.fit: Daytime outdoor dancing with a world-class DJ and you are home before bedtime - exactly the shape of the BQE day party he loved, but with a better booth. Sunday afternoon is his best slot and this is the last real chance before the season closes.

candidates.title: Refuge Saturday: Floating Points
candidates.summary: Floating Points plays a Saturday night at Refuge on Scholes Street the night before his Mister Sunday set, per RA's artist page and Songkick's listing of his tour dates. I could not open the individual event page, so time and price are unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: Same artist, smaller room, late night - the version of this weekend for when he wants the night set rather than the sunshine set. Flagging it so he can pick one and not accidentally miss both.

candidates.title: P.E.A.R.L., Anastasia Kristensen, Juana
candidates.summary: Public Records runs all three rooms - Sound Room, Atrium and Upstairs - on Friday Oct 23 from 11pm, with P.E.A.R.L. and Juana in the club room and Anastasia Kristensen alongside. Hard, European-leaning techno in the best-sounding small room in Brooklyn. Price not listed on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: Gowanus is fifteen minutes from Fort Greene and the Sound Room is the under-200-people, see-the-DJ's-face room he keeps asking for. This is the Berlin-adjacent techno night without having to go to a warehouse in Queens.

candidates.title: Echo Chamber S1.E04: Sinai Sound System feat. Lasai
candidates.summary: Fourth episode of Public Records' Echo Chamber series, with Sinai Sound System and Lasai in the Sound Room, Thursday Oct 22 at 10:30pm. Dub and sound-system music on a rig built for exactly that. Ticket price not published on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: His Thursday slot, in a 200-capacity room, run as a series rather than a marketed club night - the sort of thing you only know about because you follow the venue. Low commitment if he wants to be home by 1.

candidates.title: Franc Moody (DJ set), Cody Currie open to close, Cosmo, Pei Up
candidates.summary: Elsewhere gives over the full venue on Friday Oct 23 from 10:30pm to Franc Moody's DJ set and an open-to-close from London house producer Cody Currie, plus Cosmo and Pei Up. Multi-room Bushwick club with a rooftop. Price shows on the Eventbrite link.
candidates.fit: Disco-leaning house in Bushwick, a neighborhood he already drinks in, with the option to move between rooms instead of being stuck in one crowd. Good fallback if Knockdown feels like too much of a trek on a Friday.

candidates.title: Nowadays Nonstop: Ayesha, Mor Elian, Pearson Sound, BEARCAT, Baby Leo, Tasha
candidates.time_text: starts Saturday night and runs straight through Sunday
candidates.summary: Nowadays' Nonstop format runs from Saturday night through Sunday with no closing time; this edition has Ayesha, Mor Elian, Pearson Sound, BEARCAT, Baby Leo, Tasha and The Untouchables, covering dub, hardgroove, jungle and 140. Listed on RA's Nowadays club page; I could not open the individual event page for the exact start time or price.
candidates.fit: The trick with Nonstop as a dad is that you can show up at noon on Sunday and walk into a full dance floor in daylight - no 2am required. Same weekend as Mister Sunday, so he can pick the one that fits the babysitter.

candidates.title: Diva Diva: PAURRO & Kiernan Laveaux, Saia & e-Lite, with Willow Pill
candidates.summary: Sunday afternoon party in the Atrium at Public Records with DJs PAURRO, Kiernan Laveaux, Saia and e-Lite plus a performance by Willow Pill. Starts at 4pm. Price not published on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: Drag plus DJs in a small room, in daylight, fifteen minutes from his door - the daytime cousin of the Phoenix drag nights he does with the guys. Also an easy sell for a date night that does not require a 1am commitment.

candidates.title: 233 Record Fair, co-hosted by Shawn Dub
candidates.summary: Record fair in the Garden and Nursery at Public Records on Saturday Oct 24 from 11am, co-hosted by Shawn Dub. Outdoor, daytime, with the cafe and Atrium open. Entry price not published on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: Saturday-morning digging in an open-air nursery, stroller fits, and the adults are genuinely entertained - the rare daytime thing that is about music rather than about being somewhere with a kid.

candidates.title: Elsewhere Halloween: Major League DJz, SAIDAH, D Stone
candidates.summary: Elsewhere's Halloween night takes over the full venue on Saturday Oct 31 from 10:30pm with South Africa's Major League DJz headlining, plus SAIDAH and D Stone. Major League DJz are the Balcony Mix duo who exported amapiano worldwide. Price on the Eventbrite link.
candidates.fit: Amapiano's biggest exports playing a costume night in Bushwick - that is the Afrobeats phase and the dress-up-with-friends thing in one booking. Book this one now; it is the single best Halloween pick in this lane.

candidates.title: Bonobo (DJ Set)
candidates.summary: Bonobo plays a DJ set at Knockdown Center on the night of Saturday Dec 5 into Sunday Dec 6, starting around 11pm. Dice's venue page lists it as Sat Dec 5; doNYC lists it as Sun Dec 6 at 11pm, which is the same night either way. Price unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: Melodic, warm, builds for an hour before it drops - the Tinlicker and Marsh part of his taste played by someone who has been doing it for twenty years. Tickets for Bonobo DJ sets in New York disappear, so this is a book-now item.

candidates.title: The Blaze (Live)
candidates.summary: French duo The Blaze play a live show at Knockdown Center on Wednesday Oct 28 at 7pm, listed on Dice's venue page, doNYC and Bandsintown. Live electronic rather than a DJ set. Ticket price unconfirmed - I could not open the individual event page.
candidates.fit: Emotional, melodic, build-and-release electronic music played live - the same nerve the Kx5 show hit. It is a Wednesday, which normally disqualifies it, but an early 7pm start means he can be home at a reasonable hour.

candidates.title: Papi Juice Halloween
candidates.summary: Papi Juice, the long-running Brooklyn collective party, takes the full venue at Elsewhere on Friday Oct 30 at 10:30pm for its Halloween edition. Listed on Elsewhere's official calendar; price on the Eventbrite link.
candidates.fit: Community-run, word-of-mouth, zero marketing budget, and a dance floor that actually dances - the opposite of a listicle party. Friday night, costumes, Bushwick.

candidates.title: MPH - New York, Forever
candidates.summary: UK producer MPH headlines a Knockdown Center main-hall night on Saturday Nov 28 at 10pm, listed on Dice's venue page and Bandsintown. Price unconfirmed - I could not open the individual event page.
candidates.fit: Big-room UK house and garage on a holiday-weekend Saturday, which is the kind of night where a crew that never gets out all shows up. Warehouse, not a club with a guest list.

candidates.title: Mousse T.
candidates.summary: German house producer Mousse T. plays the Atrium at Public Records on Thursday Nov 5 at 10:30pm. The Atrium is the smaller room on the campus - a few hundred people at most. Price not published on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: A German house institution in a room where he can talk to the bartender, on a Thursday, a short ride from Fort Greene. German artists touring New York are a standing yes and this is one in the right size room.

candidates.title: DAX J (Open to Close)
candidates.summary: Berlin-based techno DJ Dax J plays open to close at Knockdown Center on Saturday Nov 14, listed on the venue's calendar and doNYC. One DJ for the whole night in the main hall. Price unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: Berghain-school techno from a Berlin resident, done properly as a single all-night set. This is the big-room version of the Berlin night; the Public Records bookings are the small-room version.

candidates.title: DJ Harvey (Extended Set)
candidates.summary: DJ Harvey plays an extended set at Knockdown Center on Friday Nov 13, per the venue's own calendar and doNYC. Harvey is a disco and house institution who only plays long sets. Start time and price unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: One DJ, one room, all night, no opener filler - the format where you actually hear a set develop rather than a parade of 60-minute slots. Worth booking ahead because Harvey nights in New York go.

candidates.title: Benji B, Cosmo, Louise Chen, Hidden Spheres
candidates.summary: Public Records runs the Sound Room, Atrium and Upstairs on Saturday Nov 7 from 11pm with Benji B headlining, plus Cosmo, Louise Chen, Hidden Spheres, Francis Harris and Tal. Price not published on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: Benji B's whole thing is moving between hip-hop, broken beat and house in one set, which maps onto how his library actually looks. Small rooms, serious sound, twenty minutes from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: Shelter: Timmy Regisford Open To Close
candidates.summary: Timmy Regisford brings his legendary Shelter party to the Sound Room at Public Records on Sunday Nov 22, starting at 3pm and playing open to close. New York house history in a 200-capacity room. Price not published on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: A Sunday afternoon, a 200-person room, and one of the actual founders of New York house music playing every record himself. This is the 'you had to know someone to hear about it' pick of the radar window.

candidates.title: Cinthie, Amir Alexander, Snad, Jenifa Mayanja, Edan
candidates.summary: Berlin house DJ and label owner Cinthie headlines all three rooms at Public Records on Saturday Nov 28 with Amir Alexander, Snad, Jenifa Mayanja and Edan. Thanksgiving-weekend Saturday. Price not published on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: Berlin again, but the warm house side rather than the hammering techno side - closer to what he actually plays at home. Thanksgiving Saturday is a night the guys are all in town.

candidates.title: Giant Rooks
candidates.summary: German band Giant Rooks, from Hamm, play Brooklyn Steel on Friday Nov 13 as part of their North American tour. Listed on JamBase and the Brooklyn Paper venue calendar. 1,800-capacity room; exact time and price unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: A German band he can sing along to in a room that is not an arena - the German-music lane without having to wait for Seeed or Deichkind to finally cross the Atlantic. Williamsburg, so he is already in the neighborhood on training days.

candidates.title: The Atrium: Eli Escobar, Jen Cardini
candidates.summary: Sunday afternoon in the Atrium at Public Records on Nov 29 with New York's Eli Escobar and Berlin-based French DJ Jen Cardini, starting at 4pm. Small room, daytime, Thanksgiving weekend. Price not published on the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: Sunday-afternoon dancing in a small room on the last day of the long weekend, finished early enough to be useful. Jen Cardini is the Berlin-by-way-of-Paris sound; Escobar is pure New York.

candidates.title: Polymarket UFC 334: Gane vs. Hokit
candidates.time_text: ticket listings show a 5pm first bell for early prelims; the main card runs late evening
candidates.summary: UFC's annual Garden card returns Saturday, November 14, with two title fights on top: heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane defending against undefeated American Josh Hokit. MSG's own event page and UFC.com both list the date and venue; ESPN and Tapology show a 13-fight card. Ticket prices were not confirmed, so check MSG directly before you buy.
candidates.fit: This is the one big-spectacle fight night of the fall for him: a real UFC pay-per-view at the Garden, the exception to his no-tourist-Manhattan rule, and the kind of plan he can put in the group chat a month out. Buy early; the Garden card is the only major combat-sports event confirmed in the city between now and early December.

candidates.title: WWE RAW & SmackDown: Two Shows, One Night
candidates.summary: Barclays Center's own events listing shows a WWE doubleheader taping, RAW and SmackDown back to back, on Monday, November 2. One ticket covers both shows. Start time and prices were not confirmed.
candidates.fit: Live pro wrestling is squarely in his weird-spectacle lane and this one is a ten-minute walk from Fort Greene, which is the only reason a Monday is worth it. It is loud, dumb in the right way, and a good guys' night that still gets him home at a reasonable hour.

candidates.title: Flex Fights MMA
candidates.time_text: state commission listing shows an approximate 6pm fighter report time; doors are later
candidates.summary: The New York State Athletic Commission's event calendar lists a Flex Fights MMA card at HK Hall on West 48th Street on Friday, November 6. It is a small-room local MMA show sanctioned by the state, not a televised promotion. No ticket link or price was confirmed.
candidates.fit: Small room, local fighters, no marketing budget: closer to the secret-you-had-to-know-about register than an arena card, and an easy Friday with one friend from the gym. Worth a look only if the matchmaking is decent, so check the card before you commit.

candidates.title: RAW WINE New York 2026
candidates.price_text: around $70 for a one-day public ticket online, $90 at the door, $110 for both days (2025 pricing; confirm 2026 on the site)
candidates.summary: RAW WINE is Isabelle Legeron's travelling natural wine fair and the North American edition lands in Brooklyn on November 8 and 9 at Five-Two-A in Industry City. Hundreds of small organic, biodynamic and low-intervention growers pour their own wine and you talk to the person who made it. Sunday is the better public day; Monday skews trade.
candidates.fit: This is the natural wine fair version of what he likes about a good bar: you talk to the maker, not a brand rep. It is a Sunday daytime thing in Brooklyn, which fits his weekend-daytime slot, and it works either as a guys' plan or a date with his wife.

candidates.title: Brewminaries Beer & Ferm Fest at Strong Rope Brewery
candidates.summary: A beer-and-fermentation festival in the Red Hook taproom on Sunday November 8, 1pm to 5pm, with tickets starting around $44.95. It is a small-room, waterfront-brewery format rather than a convention hall.
candidates.fit: Strong Rope in Red Hook on a good day is already one of his favourite hangs, so this is his bar doing something he has not done there. Afternoon, four hours, home well before bedtime.

candidates.title: Boos & Brews: Halloween Beer & Candy Pairing at Queue
candidates.summary: A guided Halloween beer-and-candy pairing at Queue in Brooklyn on Wednesday October 28 at 7pm, $50 per person. Seated, structured, and deliberately stupid in a good way.
candidates.fit: Exactly the kind of oddball bar programming he likes more than a themed club night, and it is small enough to talk to whoever is pouring. Downside: it is a Wednesday, so it only works if he is up for a midweek.

candidates.title: Marlowe Artisanal Ales 7th Anniversary Party at Queue Beer
candidates.price_text: free entry, pay for what you drink
candidates.summary: Marlowe celebrates seven years with an all-day takeover of Queue Beer in Brooklyn on Saturday October 24, noon to 11pm, free to walk in. Expect a deep draft list of their own stuff plus one-offs.
candidates.fit: Small Brooklyn brewery, small bar, no ticket, no line. This is the drop-in option if the Saturday plan needs to stay loose, and it pairs well with Blocktoberfest earlier the same afternoon.

candidates.title: 4th Avenue Pub 20th Anniversary Party
candidates.summary: One of Brooklyn's longest-running serious beer bars turns twenty on Thursday October 22, with the party starting at 4pm and no cover. Expect rare kegs pulled for the occasion.
candidates.fit: A Thursday-night, ten-minute ride from Fort Greene, in a dark back-garden bar rather than anything with a guest list. Low effort, easy to get two or three guys to show up.

candidates.title: The Lineup Dinner Series
candidates.price_text: five courses with five wines; price varies by dinner, budget well over $100 a head
candidates.summary: The Lineup is a one-night-only Brooklyn dinner series that hands the kitchen to sous chefs from serious New York restaurants (Lilia among them) to cook their own five-course, five-wine menu. It runs out of the Food52 space on Lorimer Street in Williamsburg.
candidates.fit: This is the chef-collab format he actually wants: a real cook running his own menu for one night in a small room, not a restaurant-week prix fixe. Worth following so he is the one who gets the six seats when the next date drops.

candidates.title: Marc 179 monthly chef pop-up (Marc Murphy)
candidates.summary: Chef Marc Murphy runs a monthly one-night pop-up series under the Marc 179 name, with a guest chef and a themed four-course menu each time. The September 2026 edition was a German Oktoberfest menu with Sunny Anderson and unlimited beer.
candidates.fit: A monthly guest-chef dinner with a theme is his sweet spot, and the fact that they already did a proper German night rather than a frat Oktoberfest is a good sign. Put it on the watch list and grab the October or November date when it posts.

candidates.title: Queens Night Market
candidates.address: Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Queens, NY
candidates.summary: Up to a hundred vendors sell street food from around the world at Flushing Meadows on Saturdays, 4pm to midnight, with nearly everything priced at $6 or less. The season runs through the fall but the exact closing Saturday is not confirmed for 2026.
candidates.fit: Cheap, enormous, no reservations, and genuinely a community thing rather than a listicle thing. It works as a late-afternoon family outing with the one-year-old before it gets dark and crowded, or as a grazing run with the guys.

candidates.title: Maccabee Bar (Hanukkah pop-up)
candidates.price_text: cocktails, walk-in or reservation depending on the night
candidates.summary: The Hanukkah-themed cocktail pop-up he liked returns for the holiday each year. Hanukkah 2026 begins the evening of December 4, so the run should fall at the very end of the radar window and into mid-December. I could not load the site this week to confirm dates, venue or booking.
candidates.fit: He has already been and loved it, and it is the one Jewish-culture bar night that is actually a bar night. Watch the site in November; the good tables go when the announcement drops.

candidates.title: Switch n' Play Presents: Slash n' Spray
candidates.summary: Switch n' Play, the drag and burlesque collective that has been running since 2006 and is the longest-running drag show in Brooklyn, does its Halloween edition at littlefield. Core members plus guests, 21+, doors at 7 and show at 8. Tickets run roughly $19 to $25 on Eventbrite.
candidates.fit: He already does drag shows at Phoenix with the guys and loved Company XIV's Halloween burlesque; this is the same register but community-run, cheap, and over by 10 so it works as a Saturday opener or a date night.

candidates.title: Petite Rouge — Company XIV
candidates.time_text: Thu, Fri and Sat at 8pm; Sun at 6pm
candidates.price_text: from $35 Thursday, from $39 Sunday, from $49 Friday and Saturday
candidates.summary: Company XIV's world-premiere Little Red Riding Hood burlesque is in its final two weeks at Théâtre XIV before it closes October 31 and the room flips to Nutcracker Rouge. Circus, opera, dance and striptease in their own Bushwick cabaret, 21+, with table and couch seating plus a cocktail program. Seats start around $35 and climb on weekend nights.
candidates.fit: Company XIV is his favorite room in the city and this is the last window to catch Petite Rouge before it's gone; the Sunday 6pm show is the easy babysitter math, the Thursday 8pm is the standard date night.

candidates.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show shadow cast + Time Warp After Dark
candidates.time_text: 7pm trivia pre-show, 8pm screening, DJ party after until 1am
candidates.price_text: screening free with reservation; the after-party is ticketed
candidates.summary: brooklynONE productions runs its annual Rocky Horror shadow cast in Industry City's courtyard: trivia with prizes at 7, a fully interactive shadowcast screening with prop bags at 8, a Frank-N-Furter look-alike contest, and a Tim Curry tribute. Admission to the screening is free but you reserve through ThunderTix. The night turns into the ticketed Time Warp After Dark DJ party with DJ Dmitri until 1am.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for Rocky Horror in Flatbush and liked it; this is the bigger, free, costume-mandatory Brooklyn version with a DJ party attached, which is exactly the kind of thing you bring three friends to.

candidates.title: The Funhouse at Nitehawk Williamsburg
candidates.time_text: late show; Nitehawk's midnite weekend screenings seat around 11:45pm
candidates.summary: Tobe Hooper's 1981 carnival slasher on the Nitehawk calendar for Friday the 23rd, with food and drinks served during the film. Nitehawk's weekend midnite screenings seat just before midnight.
candidates.fit: The occasional late night he allows himself, and a cult horror print in a 90-seat room is a better use of it than a bar.

candidates.title: Young Frankenstein at Nitehawk Williamsburg
candidates.time_text: check showtimes on the Nitehawk calendar
candidates.summary: Nitehawk runs Mel Brooks's Young Frankenstein both days of the weekend as part of its Halloween programming, with full dinner and cocktail service to your seat. Tobe Hooper's carnival slasher The Funhouse plays the night before, on the 23rd.
candidates.fit: A repertory print with dinner in your lap beats a restaurant reservation for a low-effort date night, and Williamsburg is already his gym neighborhood.

candidates.title: Adam Cayton-Holland Stares Wistfully Toward the Horizon
candidates.summary: A touring hour from Adam Cayton-Holland in Union Hall's 189-seat basement room. Early Friday start, bar upstairs. Charlie Bardey's The Promise of the Hearth, Part I runs the same night in the same room if the later slot suits you better.
candidates.fit: A real touring comic in a room the size of a living room, which beats any theater show for him, and Park Slope is a short hop from Fort Greene for a Friday that starts and ends early.

candidates.title: TJ Miller: The Alien Everywhere II special taping
candidates.summary: TJ Miller tapes his Alien Everywhere tour special at littlefield across two sets the same night, 21+. Taping crowds get the tighter hour and the room is a few hundred people, not a theater.
candidates.fit: A special taping in a small Gowanus room is the version of a name comic he'd actually sit through, and the 9pm set leaves room for dinner first.

candidates.title: David Cross with Sean Patton, H. Jon Benjamin, Ike Ufomadu and Reggie Conquest
candidates.summary: David Cross headlines a stacked Tuesday bill at the Bell House with Sean Patton, H. Jon Benjamin, Ike Ufomadu and Reggie Conquest. One ballroom, no two-drink-minimum club nonsense.
candidates.fit: Normally a Tuesday is a no, but a lineup like this in Gowanus instead of a theater is the exception clause; check the Bell House site for whether seats are left before you text anyone.

candidates.title: Drunk Bollywood Live!
candidates.summary: The live Drunk Bollywood show at the Bell House, the Drunk History format applied to Hindi cinema, with performers getting progressively less coherent on stage. Early Saturday start at 7:30.
candidates.fit: This is the bar-with-weird-programming lane he keeps asking for: a format show in a Brooklyn ballroom, cheap, early, and easy to bring two friends to.

candidates.title: Ginger Snaps — Spooky Season brunch screening
candidates.summary: The cult Canadian werewolf movie Ginger Snaps screens at 11am both Saturday and Sunday at Nitehawk's Prospect Park theater, with brunch and drinks served in-seat. Part of their Spooky Season run.
candidates.fit: Weekend daytime is his other real slot; an 11am horror brunch across from Prospect Park gets him out and back before the afternoon nap window closes.

candidates.title: Nutcracker Rouge — Company XIV
candidates.time_text: evening performances, with weekend matinees added in December
candidates.price_text: on sale now; Petite Rouge seats run $35 to $59 as a reference point
candidates.summary: Company XIV's baroque-burlesque Nutcracker opens November 12 and runs through January 30 at their own Bushwick theater. Tickets and the presale are live on the Company XIV site. Champagne couches and two-top banquettes sell out first in December.
candidates.fit: The Nutcracker at Lincoln Center is his favorite night in the city and Company XIV is his favorite room; this is both at once, fifteen minutes from his door. Book the December dates now, they go.

candidates.title: Divination at Théâtre XIV: lipstick and tarot readings
candidates.price_text: half off through October per the venue's October Kiss promotion
candidates.summary: Company XIV runs French Kiss lipstick readings and tarot appointments in the bar at Théâtre XIV, booked separately through Eventbrite and timed around performances. The October Kiss promotion has them at half price this month.
candidates.fit: A cheap, genuinely odd add-on to a Company XIV date night that most people who go to the show never even notice is on offer.

candidates.title: George Balanchine's The Nutcracker — New York City Ballet
candidates.time_text: evenings plus weekend matinees once the run starts
candidates.venue: David H. Koch Theater, Lincoln Center
candidates.summary: NYCB's Nutcracker is the late-November-to-early-January fixture at the Koch Theater. I could not load the NYCB site this week, so the 2026 opening date, performance calendar and current price tiers are unconfirmed here.
candidates.fit: He says this was the single best night he has had in the city, and the good seats for the weekend performances go early; treat this as a reminder to pull up the calendar and book, not as a verified listing.

candidates.title: Lightscape at Brooklyn Botanic Garden
candidates.summary: BBG's winter light trail typically opens in mid-to-late November and runs on timed-entry tickets through early January. I could not load the BBG site this week, so the 2026 opening date and ticket prices are unconfirmed here.
candidates.fit: He has done it and liked it, and the early-season weeknight slots are the ones worth grabbing before the December crowds; check the on-sale date yourself this week.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Museum First Saturday
candidates.summary: The museum's free monthly First Saturday night turns the galleries into a party with DJs, live performance and a bar. The November edition falls on the 7th. I could not load the museum site this week, so the lineup and any ticketed elements are unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: Free, walkable from Fort Greene, DJs in a museum rather than a club, and the kind of crowd that makes it feel like an art opening that got out of hand; confirm the November program before you commit the group chat.

candidates.title: NYC Century Bike Tour
candidates.time_text: rolling start from 6am, event runs to 6pm
candidates.summary: Transportation Alternatives' NYC Century returns Sunday Oct 25, with 40, 55, 75 and 100-mile routes stitched together from greenways, parks and city streets across four boroughs. Organizer page lists a 6am to 6pm window; registration is $130 general and $205 VIP (guaranteed first wave, t-shirt, finisher medal). Route maps and start details live on nyccentury.org.
candidates.fit: He rode Lower Manhattan to the GW Bridge with friends and loved it; this is that ride with 2,000 other people, aid stations and a mileage option for whoever in the crew is soft. The 40 or 55 gets him home by early afternoon, which matters with a 1-year-old.

candidates.title: Cars & Coffee x Retromobile NYC
candidates.venue: Greene Street (NYC Car Club x Retromobile NYC)
candidates.summary: NYC Car Club and Retromobile NYC park up on the Greene Street cobblestones in SoHo on Saturday Oct 24, 9am to noon, rain or shine. All makes and models, three parking areas between Broome and Prince, free to attend and explicitly all ages. Organizer rules: no revving, no racing, it's a hang.
candidates.fit: This is the Daikoku-adjacent thing he keeps asking for: a real enthusiast meet, not a corny dealership lot. Cobblestones in SoHo at 9am is also the rare car event you can roll a stroller through, so the kid gets to stare at engines before lunch.

candidates.title: g.d.m Fall Moto Festival powered by Can-Am
candidates.summary: Gotham Depot Moto, the private moto storage facility on Box Street in Greenpoint, throws a fall riding-season party on Saturday Oct 24 from 11am to 4pm: moto market, music, food, raffles and Can-Am demo rides. Listed on the NYC Motorcyclist community calendar as a public event; no ticket price posted.
candidates.fit: Motorcycle-shop culture in a working Greenpoint garage is exactly the deep-scene version of car culture he wants, and it's a 20-minute drive from Fort Greene. Easy to stack with the SoHo cars and coffee earlier the same morning.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Bathhouse Presents: Masquerade Halloween Party
candidates.price_text: tickets on Eventbrite, price not shown on the listing we read
candidates.summary: The fifth edition of Brooklyn Bathhouse's monthly party, Halloween version: Friday Oct 30, 7 to 11:30pm, two live DJs, saunas, steam room, pools and a cold room, masks encouraged, 21+. It's a small independent bathhouse on Flatbush Ave, not a chain, and the café is currently closed for renovation.
candidates.fit: Costume night plus DJs plus a cold plunge is the overlap of three things he already does: the Rocky Horror dress-up, the Russian bathhouse day, and dance nights with the guys. Under 200 people, run by the house, zero bottle-service energy.

candidates.title: Aufguss sauna ceremony at Bathhouse Atlantic Ave
candidates.time_text: ceremonies daily at 12pm, 1:30, 3, 4:30, 6, 7:30 and 9pm; open 8am to 11:30pm
candidates.summary: Bathhouse opened a 32,000 sq ft Atlantic Avenue location in May 2026 in the shadow of Barclays, with thermal pools, cold plunges, steam and a large event sauna. Aufguss ceremonies, where a sauna master works the heat with towel routines, essential oils and music, run seven times a day at no extra cost on top of the day pass, which starts at $29. Booking is through bathhouseatlanticave.try.be.
candidates.fit: A full bathhouse day with a friend is one of his favorite things, and this one is a 15-minute walk from Fort Greene instead of a trip to the East Village. Time the visit to land on a 6pm or 7:30pm Aufguss so it's a performance, not just sitting in a hot room.

candidates.title: Halloween Fest and the Great PUPkin Dog Costume Contest
candidates.address: Monument Plaza, Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn
candidates.summary: Fort Greene Park Conservancy and NYC Parks run Halloween Fest at Monument Plaza on Saturday Oct 24, noon to 4pm, with spooky stories, face painting and games. The Great PUPkin dog costume contest, a long-running Fort Greene institution, happens inside it from noon to 1pm. Free, no RSVP, rain date Oct 25.
candidates.fit: Literally his front yard, costumes on the toddler, done by mid-afternoon, and the PUPkin is the kind of neighborhood tradition that's actually funny for the adults. Show up at noon for the dogs and leave when the kid melts down.

candidates.title: TWA Hotel rooftop pool day pass
candidates.time_text: non-hotel guests 11am to 11pm; reservations are 1 hour 45 minutes
candidates.address: One Idlewild Drive, JFK Airport, Queens, NY 11430
candidates.price_text: from $50 per adult for non-hotel guests; $25 gym day pass if you want shower and locker access
candidates.summary: The rooftop infinity pool over JFK's runway 4L/22R is open year round and is heated to about 95 degrees in winter, with the Pool Bar serving daily 11am to 11pm. Non-hotel guests book through ResortPass; cover starts at $50 for adults, each reservation is one hour 45 minutes, and reservations are required through Nov 1. Loungers can't be reserved and showers aren't included.
candidates.fit: He's done this on a summer day and loved it; the cold-weather version, sitting in a 95-degree pool in the open air while 777s climb out, is the better version and nobody he knows has done it in October. Good wife plan with dinner at the hotel after.

candidates.title: World Spa day pass and Grand Banya
candidates.time_text: open daily, late hours on weekends
candidates.summary: World Spa is a 50,000 sq ft bathhouse in south Brooklyn with 16 thermal rooms including the largest banya in the US, Turkish hammams, Japanese onsen pools and Finnish saunas, plus restaurants on site. Day passes start at $99. The German-built banya heater gets a ceremonial bucket rotation with herb-infused water every few hours.
candidates.fit: The upgrade on the Russian and Turkish Baths day he loved: same venik-and-plunge ritual, ten times the square footage, and you can spend six hours there with one friend and still have rooms you haven't tried. Book a parenie treatment if he wants the full beating-with-oak-branches version.

candidates.title: QC Spa New York on Governors Island
candidates.time_text: open daily, roughly 10am to 10pm with later hours Friday and Saturday; sunset and full-day entries available
candidates.price_text: around $142 and up per person depending on entry time; book direct at booking.qcny.com
candidates.summary: QC's Governors Island spa runs heated outdoor courtyard pools, timber saunas, steam rooms and relaxation rooms inside restored brick officers' housing, five minutes by ferry from Lower Manhattan, 21+. Their current fall programming leans into the outdoor pools with the skyline and fall color behind them, with food and wine included in some packages. Third-party sellers list entry from about $142 up to about $204 for a full day; check the direct booking page for the real price on a given date.
candidates.fit: A spa you have to take a boat to is the kind of small adventure he likes more than the spa itself, and the heated outdoor pools in late October are better than in August. Date night, phones in the locker, ferry back at night.

candidates.title: SWEAT: a sauna and sound pop-up by CUL DE SAC
candidates.time_text: afternoon into evening sessions, 25-minute sauna rounds
candidates.address: Avenue C and E 9th St, New York, NY
candidates.summary: CUL DE SAC turns a community garden in the East Village into an open-air bathhouse: wood-fired sauna that fits 18 to 20 people per 25-minute round, cold plunge, rotating DJs, food and drinks. Editions run on weekends and sell out; recent ones were listed at $25, 18+. The autumn run listed on doNYC ran Sep 28 through Oct 19, so the next dates need confirming on their Eventbrite or RA page.
candidates.fit: Eighteen people in a wood-fired sauna in a community garden with a DJ is the most word-of-mouth thing in this lane, and it costs less than a round of drinks. Exactly the opposite of the chain bathhouse experience.

candidates.title: Elahni sauna and ice bath sessions
candidates.price_text: $39 for the 30-minute self-guided Reset, $65 for the 70-minute hosted Signature
candidates.summary: Elahni bills itself as a wellness speakeasy: a small, semi-private Finnish sauna and cold plunge room in Manhattan with two formats, a 30-minute self-guided Reset at $39 a seat and a 70-minute hosted Signature at $65. Guides walk you through the rounds. Capacity is tiny compared with Bathhouse or Othership.
candidates.fit: Small room, no scene, book it for two and talk to the person running it; it's the sauna equivalent of the hidden bars he already likes. Good weeknight option when a full bathhouse day isn't on.

candidates.title: Candlelit Restorative Free Flow at Othership Flatiron
candidates.summary: Othership runs a candlelit version of its 75-minute Free Flow at the Flatiron location on Sunday Oct 25: self-guided rounds between the sauna and the ice baths with guides on hand, built around deep rest rather than the usual music-led class. Reservations go through the Othership schedule page; drop-in pricing isn't listed on the event page.
candidates.fit: The quiet one, for a Sunday evening with his wife rather than the guys. Their Williamsburg room is the closer option on a normal week; note their NYC calendar is heavy on singles socials, which is not his email.

candidates.title: TCS New York City Marathon
candidates.time_text: first waves start 8am; Brooklyn runners come through late morning
candidates.venue: TCS New York City Marathon course
candidates.summary: The 2026 marathon runs Sunday Nov 1 with the first start at 8am. The course crosses Brooklyn through Fort Greene and Clinton Hill in the morning before heading north, and spectating is free anywhere on the route. The Abbott Dash to the Finish Line 5K on Oct 31 is already sold out, so running it yourself this year is off the table.
candidates.fit: The loudest free party in his neighborhood: stand on the curb with coffee and the kid in the carrier, friends welcome, done by lunch. He doesn't need a ticket or a plan, just a corner.

candidates.title: NYRR Ted Corbitt 15K
candidates.summary: The 18th annual Ted Corbitt 15K runs Saturday Dec 5 at 8am in Central Park, honoring the father of American long-distance running. Registration through NYRR is listed at $45 plus a $2.58 processing fee, or $35 plus fees for members. It's a proper race with a real organizer, not a social run club.
candidates.fit: He asked for races with an organizer, not run clubs that are dating apps. A cold 15K in the park with one friend, finished by 9:30am, is a good excuse for a December Saturday, and it needs booking now before it fills.

candidates.title: Safe Streets Social (Transportation Alternatives)
candidates.price_text: ticketed through Zeffy, price not listed on the organizer page
candidates.summary: The closing party of Transportation Alternatives' Vision Zero Cities conference, Thursday Oct 29 from 5:30 to 8pm: STUF'D food truck, drinks, live music from Pondless, and test rides on Lime, Veo and Upway e-bikes and scooters. Included free with conference registration, otherwise ticketed separately through Zeffy. The organizer page doesn't list the venue address, so check the ticket page before committing.
candidates.fit: A Thursday-night room full of people who actually build the city's streets, with a food truck and bikes to ride, not a networking mixer with name tags. Low-commitment if the guys bail; skip if the venue turns out to be a conference hall.

candidates.title: Bikes and Breakfast, City Island
candidates.price_text: free to attend, you buy your own breakfast
candidates.summary: Bikes and Breakfast is a long-running vintage and classic motorcycle gathering that meets the first Sunday of the month in Palisades, the second Sunday on City Island in the Bronx and the third Sunday in Cold Spring, 8am to 11am. The City Island edition falls on Sunday Nov 8. It's a show-up-and-talk-shop meet with no ticket; confirm on their site, since attendance thins once the weather turns.
candidates.fit: Old bikes, a sea-town main street in the Bronx and coffee by 8am: a car-and-moto scene thing with zero marketing, which is what he's after. Easy to bring the kid, easy to be home before the nap.

candidates.title: Repertory at Goethe: Christoph Schlingensief's Germany Trilogy
candidates.summary: The German Film Office screens all three parts of Schlingensief's gory reunification-era Germany Trilogy at the Goethe-Institut on Saturday October 24 at 3pm, introduced by curator Steve Macfarlane. Free, registration required, first come first served.
candidates.fit: German culture plus Halloween-season splatter in a small screening room, with an intro from a curator who knows the material. Exactly the kind of German programming he says he wants, and it is free on a Saturday afternoon.

candidates.title: Zombie Films: German Halloween Double Feature at Goethe
candidates.summary: The German Film Office and Goethe-Institut New York program a Halloween double feature of German zombie favorites on Thursday Oct 29, 7–10pm. Same small Irving Place screening room as the Schlingensief marathon. The listing shows date and time but no price.
candidates.fit: A Thursday-night German horror double bill two days before Halloween, with the guys, in a 100-seat room - not a Times Square multiplex and not a Time Out Halloween roundup.

candidates.title: America's Liberal Reckoning: A Munk Debate at 92NY (Fareed Zakaria vs Patrick Deneen)
candidates.summary: The Munk Debates come to New York for the first time, co-hosted with 92NY, days after the midterms. Motion: be it resolved, liberalism has failed America. Fareed Zakaria argues against, Notre Dame political philosopher Patrick Deneen argues for, Rudyard Griffiths moderates. Munk lists 7:00pm and 92NY's own calendar shows Thu Nov 12; one aggregator lists 7:30pm, so check your ticket.
candidates.fit: This is the high-caliber ideas night he actually wants: a real one-on-one debate with named heavyweights, on a Thursday, not a panel of nobodies. Book it now - the first Munk in New York will sell.

candidates.title: Hanukkah Klezmer Concert & Party: Jake Shulman-Ment, Alicia Svigals & Pete Rushefsky
candidates.summary: Same series, Hanukkah edition: violinist Jake Shulman-Ment, Klezmatics co-founder Alicia Svigals and tsimbl player Pete Rushefsky play a concert and party at the Old Broadway Synagogue on Saturday Dec 5, 7–9pm, per CTMD's events calendar. It is billed as a party, not just a sit-down concert. No price listed yet.
candidates.fit: Holiday-season Jewish programming that is a party rather than a museum lecture, in a tiny shul, with Alicia Svigals on fiddle. Pairs with the Hanukkah bar run he already likes.

candidates.title: An Evening with Alex Weiser and Andrzej Cieplinski: Celebrating "Tfiles"
candidates.summary: Composer Alex Weiser and clarinetist Andrzej Cieplinski appear in person at the Center for Jewish History to mark Tfiles ahead of its Carnegie Hall premiere. It is an in-person program in CJH's small auditorium on West 16th Street. The calendar confirms the Oct 22 date but did not show a start time or price; CJH programs are usually free with registration.
candidates.fit: New Jewish concert music in a 200-seat room, with the composer talking you through it, on his main Thursday slot - a quieter date-night option than a bar.

candidates.title: Festival Neue Literatur: "Guests and Ghosts" + Friedrich Ulfers Prize to Peter Wortsman
candidates.summary: The 16th Festival Neue Literatur (Oct 26–29), run jointly by Deutsches Haus at NYU, the Goethe-Institut, the German, Austrian and Swiss consulates and Columbia, stages a readings-and-conversation night with German-language authors Michael Lentz, Tanja Paar and Laura Vogt plus US author Jonas Hassen Khemiri, moderated by translator Alta Price. The 2026 Friedrich Ulfers Prize goes to Peter Wortsman the same evening. Organizer listing confirms Tue Oct 27, 6:30–8pm at the Goethe-Institut.
candidates.fit: The German-language literary scene in New York in one room, free-ish and unmarketed. It is a Tuesday, so it only makes the radar - but it is the week's deepest German-culture thing.

candidates.title: Festival Neue Literatur: "Intimate Thresholds - Identity and Longing"
candidates.summary: Opening night of Festival Neue Literatur 2026: an evening of readings and conversation on identity and longing at Deutsches Haus at NYU, Monday Oct 26, 6–7:30pm, with registration through the Austrian Cultural Forum. The festival is the only one in the US that pairs new German-language fiction from Germany, Austria and Switzerland with American writers.
candidates.fit: Only worth a Monday if German literature is the hook, which for him it sometimes is - and the Washington Mews townhouse is about as small-room as New York gets.

candidates.title: AI Data Centers: Is Space the Next Frontier?
candidates.summary: Columbia's Center on Global Energy Policy hosts a public session on whether orbital data centers are a real answer to the power demands of AI, at The Forum on the Manhattanville campus, Tuesday Oct 20, 5–6pm. CGEP's events page confirms date, time and venue; no price is listed and CGEP public events are typically free with registration.
candidates.fit: Energy markets and power demand is his lane, and CGEP is the serious room for it. It is a Tuesday at 5pm, so it is a leave-work-early play rather than a night out.

candidates.title: Storage Is the New Grid: Jobs, Investment, and Community
candidates.summary: CGEP's evening program on energy storage as core grid infrastructure - investment, jobs, community - on Tuesday Nov 10, 6–9pm. The events page confirms the date and time but does not yet show a venue address or price, so confirm the location before committing.
candidates.fit: Second CGEP option on the radar if the commodities and power-markets side is what he wants that week; the 6–9pm format usually means a real reception, not a webinar.

candidates.title: Exceptional Hatred: Antisemitism and Free Speech in America, Past and Present
candidates.summary: An in-person book talk and discussion co-sponsored by the American Jewish Historical Society, the Center for Jewish History and the Shalom Hartman Institute, Wednesday Oct 21 at 7pm on West 16th Street. CJH's calendar confirms date and time; price was not shown and CJH programs in this series are generally free with registration.
candidates.fit: A Wednesday, so only if the subject grabs him - but it is a serious, non-performative Jewish-ideas evening at the best-run Jewish archive in the city, and it is a 15-minute ride from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: Yiddish Theater Walking Tour (YIVO)
candidates.time_text: start time not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: YIVO runs a guided walking tour of the old Yiddish theater district, listed at $18 with registration required on the Center for Jewish History program calendar. Heads-up: the calendar's layout made it impossible to pin the exact day and start time - it sits between the Oct 22 and Oct 25 listings - so confirm both on the registration page before planning around it.
candidates.fit: Weekend daytime, outdoors, $18, and the kind of city history that is actually interesting to the adults; a carrier-friendly option if the time works.

candidates.title: 2026 New York Jewish Book Festival and Hanukkah Bazaar
candidates.time_text: panels start 11:30am, runs through the afternoon
candidates.summary: A one-day festival at the Museum of Jewish Heritage on Sunday Nov 15: author panels across genres for all ages starting at 11:30am (Renoir's Jewish muses, New York biographies and more), plus a Hanukkah Bazaar for holiday shopping. The museum's own event page confirms the date and the schedule; ticket pricing is not shown on the listing.
candidates.fit: Sunday daytime, stroller-friendly museum with elevators, done by mid-afternoon, and the Hanukkah Bazaar gives it a reason beyond 'go to a museum.' Make it a ferry-and-Battery-Park morning with the kid.

candidates.title: Baklava Express at Barbès
candidates.summary: Balkan and Anatolian party band Baklava Express play the back room at Barbès on Thursday October 22 at 10pm, bringing sweets from Good Baklava. Barbès runs on a pass-the-hat suggested donation.
candidates.fit: Barbès is a 50-person back room where the band plays a foot from your face, which is his stated sweet spot. A good late-Thursday second stop after dinner, and nobody in his group chat will have heard of it.

candidates.title: Baklava Express at Barbès
candidates.summary: Balkan and Turkish party band Baklava Express plays the Barbès back room late on Thursday Oct 22 at 10pm, per concert listings for the venue. Barbès does not publish a web calendar - only a monthly PDF - so the time and lineup come from an aggregator rather than the bar itself.
candidates.fit: A late Thursday backup if the Deutsches Haus talk ends at 7:30 and the night still has legs: 40 minutes from Fort Greene, a tiny room, a band nobody in his group chat has heard of.

candidates.title: Slavic Soul Party! - 23-year Tuesday residency at Barbès
candidates.price_text: door charge collected in person, typically about $10 to $20
candidates.summary: The nine-piece Balkan brass band Slavic Soul Party! has played every Tuesday at 9pm in the Barbès back room for over 23 years, and the band's own calendar confirms the residency is ongoing (Oct 20, Oct 27 and Nov 10 among the listed dates). It is a standing-room brass stomp in a room that fits well under 100 people. Barbès collects a door charge in person.
candidates.fit: If he ever wants a Tuesday that justifies itself: a nine-piece brass band three feet away, no marketing budget, two decades deep. Closest thing Brooklyn has to a Berlin corner-bar institution.

candidates.title: Too Much Is Better Than Too Little: Alfred Hilsberg, ZickZack & the Invention of the German Underground
candidates.summary: An exhibition listed as currently on at the Goethe-Institut New York about Alfred Hilsberg and the ZickZack label, the people who effectively invented the German post-punk underground (Neue Deutsche Welle, Einstürzende Neubauten's world). The Goethe site lists it as ongoing but did not show opening and closing dates or hours, so check before going.
candidates.fit: German music history he genuinely cares about - the lineage behind everything Berlin - in a free gallery he can walk through before a Goethe screening. Dates unconfirmed, so call first.

candidates.title: Witches and Stitches 2026 Finale: Urban Legends
candidates.summary: The year-long drag and costume competition Witches and Stitches crowns its 2026 winner at All Night Skate on Thursday October 22, doors 8pm, $10 suggested donation. This year's final theme is urban legends and every monthly winner competes.
candidates.fit: He already loves All Night Skate and drag shows with the guys; this is the night that bar's community actually shows up for, it is ten dollars, and it is on a Thursday, his main weeknight slot.

candidates.title: The Q Brothers: Hip Hop for Families
candidates.summary: The Q Brothers do their first-ever Rock and Roll Playhouse family show at Brooklyn Bowl on Saturday October 24: improvised hip-hop with Jeff Ellis of Freestyle Love Supreme, a DJ-led family dance party, free ice cream. Doors 11am, show at noon, all ages, kids one and under free.
candidates.fit: The family pick: a real venue, hip-hop instead of toddler mush, done by 1pm, and in Williamsburg where he already trains. He can hand the kid a shaker and still enjoy the set.

candidates.title: TJ: The Alien Everywhere II (special taping)
candidates.time_text: early show 6pm doors / 7pm; late show 8:30pm doors / 9pm
candidates.summary: Tanael Joachim (TJ), fresh off an FX pilot, tapes his new hour at Littlefield on Thursday October 22 with two shows. Material is about love, death, grief and immigration; tickets through Littlefield's Eventbrite.
candidates.fit: Small-room stand-up on a Thursday, and a taping means the comic is at full effort and the room is stacked with people who care. Much better than a club show for the one-to-three friends format.

candidates.title: Petite Rouge by Company XIV (final weeks)
candidates.time_text: evening performances, check the calendar for curtain
candidates.summary: Company XIV's baroque-burlesque Little Red Riding Hood closes Halloween night; the company says only eight performances remain. Théâtre XIV in Bushwick, 21+, cocktail service at the table.
candidates.fit: Company XIV is already a favorite and their Halloween-season show was a highlight, so the closing weeks of Petite Rouge is the obvious date night before it disappears on October 31.

candidates.title: Rocky Horror Picture Show with The Occasionalists
candidates.summary: Brooklyn live-karaoke band The Occasionalists run their annual Rocky Horror night at Littlefield on Friday October 30: full band, audience singing, Rocky-themed burlesque performers including Thirty3Teeth and B4B7B1U3. Tickets via Littlefield/Eventbrite.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for Rocky Horror in Flatbush and liked it; this is the same thing but interactive, with a live band and burlesque instead of a projector. Costumes, singing, a crew of four, Friday night.

candidates.title: Farewell to America: Marc Pitzke and Gudrun Engel
candidates.time_text: evening, check the ticket page for start time
candidates.summary: Deutsches Haus at NYU and the American Council on Germany host Der Spiegel's long-time US correspondent Marc Pitzke and ARD Washington bureau chief Gudrun Engel on Thursday October 22 for a reading and conversation about Pitzke's new book on an America he no longer recognizes.
candidates.fit: German-language, serious journalists, transatlantic politics in a 60-seat room at Deutsches Haus. It is the geopolitics-talk lane and the German lane at the same time, and it's free on a Thursday.

candidates.title: P.E.A.R.L., Juana / Anastasia Kristensen
candidates.summary: Public Records' Friday October 23 programming puts techno producer P.E.A.R.L. and Juana in one room and Anastasia Kristensen alongside John Raffaele, Bob Maynard and Cassandra Croft in the other. Tickets through Dice.
candidates.fit: Small, purpose-built sound room under 200 people, serious DJs, fifteen minutes from Fort Greene. This is the counterweight to the warehouse shows: same music, room where you can talk to the bartender.

candidates.title: Between Us: Karl Haendel and Haim Steinbach in conversation
candidates.summary: Artists Karl Haendel and Haim Steinbach talk about their decades-long friendship and their very different uses of found objects and text, Thursday October 22 at 6:30pm at the Jewish Museum. Free with RSVP; their work is up in the collection show.
candidates.fit: Jewish cultural programming with two working artists rather than a panel of administrators, free, and short enough to be the first half of a Thursday night.

candidates.title: Mouthpiece: drag Thursdays at Phoenix
candidates.summary: Good Sis Productions runs Mouthpiece every Thursday at Phoenix Bar from 10pm, hosted by their resident Sis with jokes, shots and performances. It skips the first Thursday of each month. Phoenix also has new speakers and a projector and runs guest DJs on weekends.
candidates.fit: He has already had a good night at Phoenix with the guys; this is the recurring one to actually put in the calendar rather than showing up blind. Late Thursday, no cover, no bro energy.

candidates.title: PTP LIVE featuring Vontee the Singer
candidates.summary: PTP Productions brings its live R&B and rap showcase to Littlefield on Wednesday October 21 at 7pm, headlined by Vontee the Singer with a live band and DJ. Ticket link through the promoter's Instagram bio.
candidates.fit: A Wednesday, so only if he wants it: a live-band rap and R&B showcase run by a production crew rather than a venue booker, which is the kind of room where you see someone before they're a name.

candidates.title: Help Yourself: East German DIY punk, a talk by Seth Howes
candidates.summary: Goethe-Institut presents a talk by professor Seth Howes on East German punk under the Stasi, using super-8 films, cassette tapes and illegally released LPs, at the record shop Various Artists on Monday October 26 at 6:30pm. Free, part of an exhibition on Alfred Hilsberg.
candidates.fit: A record shop, forty chairs, Stasi files on punk subtypes. This is the deep German-scene material he keeps asking for, and it is a Monday he can duck out to for an hour.

candidates.title: Sō Percussion: Steve Reich's Drumming
candidates.summary: Sō Percussion and friends perform the full 75-minute Drumming at 92NY on Wednesday October 28 at 7:30pm, with Becca Stevens, Alex Sopp and others joining. $45 in person.
candidates.fit: Minimalism played live by nine people is closer to a four-hour melodic techno set than it sounds, and 92NY's hall is small and loud enough. A midweek exception worth booking, and a reasonable date night.

candidates.title: Bonobo
candidates.summary: Knockdown Center's own upcoming list has Bonobo on Saturday December 5. Tickets through Knockdown's Dice page.
candidates.fit: Melodic, warm, big-room electronic on a Saturday — the once-in-a-while spectacle slot. Worth putting on the radar now because Knockdown December dates go early.

candidates.title: Dax J
candidates.summary: Berlin-based techno DJ Dax J plays Knockdown Center on Saturday November 14 per the venue's own upcoming list. Tickets via Knockdown's Dice page.
candidates.fit: Saturday, Berlin techno, big room. One of the two or three times a year a warehouse show is worth the late night for him.

candidates.title: NY Night Train 21st Annual Haunted Hop
candidates.summary: Jonathan Toubin's long-running soul-and-garage costume party, the Haunted Hop, hits its 21st year at Knockdown Center on Friday October 30. Tickets through Knockdown's Dice page.
candidates.fit: A 21-year-old NYC costume dance party run by one DJ with a 45s bag — the opposite of a listicle Halloween event, and the costume contest means he is participating, not watching.

candidates.title: Dinner for One: Halloween Variety Spooktacular
candidates.summary: Sketch group Dinner for One does a Halloween night of sketch and stand-up at Littlefield on Thursday October 29 at 8pm with special guest Sean Patton, followed by a costume dance party with DJ Duck Soup playing 2000s hits.
candidates.fit: Thursday, small room, costumes, and it turns into a dance party instead of ending at a bar conversation. The 2000s set list is squarely his nostalgia lane.

candidates.title: Labyrinth Film Feast
candidates.time_text: evening, courses timed to the film
candidates.summary: Nitehawk Williamsburg runs a Film Feast for Labyrinth on Wednesday October 28, a multi-course menu served through the movie. The theater posted that only a few seats remain.
candidates.fit: A date night that isn't dinner-then-a-movie but both at once, in a 90-seat room. Book now because they say it's nearly gone.

candidates.title: Bela Lugosi Meets a Brooklyn Gorilla, 4K restoration
candidates.summary: Nitehawk Prospect Park screens the new 4K restoration of the 1952 oddity Bela Lugosi Meets a Brooklyn Gorilla on Thursday November 12, introduced by WFMU's Dave the Spazz, who signs his new Sammy Petrillo book at an afterparty in the downstairs lounge.
candidates.fit: Thursday, a genuinely strange film nobody has seen, and an afterparty in the bar downstairs where the guy who wrote the book is standing around. Low-key and specific.

candidates.title: Julio Torres Presents: The Cursed Amulet III
candidates.summary: Julio Torres brings back his Halloween party to Elsewhere on Wednesday October 28 with a run of DJs, surprise performances and a midnight costume competition. Tickets on sale through Elsewhere/Eventbrite.
candidates.fit: A comedian-run costume party with actual DJs, which is more interesting than a club Halloween night. Midweek, so only if the costume is already sorted.

candidates.title: Butcher's Mouth first anniversary party
candidates.summary: Butcher's Mouth celebrates one year with Fox and King at The Tiny Cupboard on Saturday November 7, 5pm to 10pm: DJs, burlesque from India Jenell and Kobradadon, handmade goods and games. RSVP link via the organizer's Instagram.
candidates.fit: Early-evening, tiny room, run by people with no marketing budget — the creative-scene party register he liked at his wife's friend's photo studio. Home by midnight.

candidates.title: Union Hall Halloween Costume Contest
candidates.summary: Union Hall runs a costume contest on its bocce courts on Saturday October 31 at 9pm, hosted by Honey Drop It, with prizes. Free to enter, RSVP on the venue site and sign up on site.
candidates.fit: The low-stakes Halloween option: bocce, a basement bar he already knows, free, and he can actually enter rather than stand around. Good fallback if the warehouse nights feel like too much.

candidates.title: George Balanchine's The Nutcracker
candidates.time_text: matinees and evenings through the run
candidates.summary: New York City Ballet's Nutcracker returns November 27 through January 2 at the Koch Theater; the company is pointing people to tickets now that the fall season has closed.
candidates.fit: He has called this one of the best things he has done in the city. The good seats on the good nights are gone by mid-November, so this is a book-it-this-week item, not a December idea.

candidates.title: Red Hook Barnacle Parade
candidates.time_text: check the organizers for step-off time
candidates.summary: The Red Hook Barnacles' annual neighborhood parade happens October 29; Strong Rope brewed this year's Barnacle King Golden Ale with Keg & Lantern and Sixpoint, with a donation to Red Hook Mutual Aid from sales. Strong Rope has six-packs now.
candidates.fit: Red Hook plus Strong Rope plus a neighborhood parade nobody outside Red Hook knows about. Easy with the kid in the carrier, and the brewery is right there afterward.

candidates.title: Bathhouse Atlantic Avenue backyard pool and outdoor sauna
candidates.summary: Bathhouse opened a heated outdoor pool and outdoor sauna in the backyard of its Atlantic Avenue location as of October 3, usable year-round with a day pass or massage booking. Lounge chairs are first come, first served.

laneReports.notes: Big caveat on this batch: my web_fetch budget ran out early in the session and then search calls started getting rate-limited, so several things I would normally have confirmed on the ticket page are marked likely rather than verified. What I actually read in full: the Public Records official calendar (publicrecords.nyc), the Elsewhere official calendar (elsewhere.club/events), RA's Nowadays club page and the RA event page for Mister Sunday, and Dice/JamBase/StubHub pages for the Massano and Ahmed Spins shows. Prices are blank on most Public Records and Elsewhere items because the venue calendars push you to Dice/Eventbrite for the number. Things I could not finish chasing, worth a look next week: (1) AXS lists a 'South House vs Naija House - Halloween Edition' at Brooklyn Steel - South African vs Nigerian house, a perfect fit - but I could not pin the date, so I left it out rather than guess; (2) Avant Gardner's events page only served me a cached 2025 calendar, so I have nothing current on the Brooklyn Mirage or the Great Hall this season; (3) RA's news index surfaced a headline saying Teksupport and its parent firm were ordered to cease operations after a legal dispute - if true that removes a major warehouse promoter from the board, and it should be confirmed before promising anything from them; (4) no deadmau5, Kx5, Eric Prydz, Kalkbrenner, Fred again.., John Summit or Disclosure New York dates surfaced in the windows I searched, and I ran out of budget before I could check Barclays, MSG, Brooklyn Paramount, Kings Theatre, Brooklyn Bowl, Good Room, Basement, The Lot Radio, Under the K Bridge or Brooklyn Storehouse - the Afrobeats/dancehall arena lane (Burna Boy, Wizkid, Asake) and the emo/ABBA/2000s themed-night lane are both unsearched and are the biggest gaps in this report; (5) Refuge on Scholes Street is included on two secondary sources only and has no ticket link I could verify.

Research was cut short. web_fetch failed on every single URL in this session (UFC.com, msg.com, barclayscenter.com, prucenter.com, boxingscene.com all returned errors), and the web_search budget was exhausted after roughly seven queries. Because I could not load a single organizer page directly, nothing here is marked verified; the strongest items are backed by organizer-page text returned inside search results. Treat every price as unconfirmed.

What I did establish: there is no major fight card in the five boroughs inside the Oct 19-25 window. The headline is UFC 334 at MSG on Sat Nov 14 (Gane vs Hokit, two title fights), confirmed independently by UFC.com, the MSG event page, ESPN and Wikipedia. Barclays Center's upcoming-events listing showed no boxing or MMA at all through the radar window, only WWE on Nov 2 and the League of Legends final on Nov 14. Prudential Center's last UFC was UFC 328 in May 2026 and nothing new is scheduled. Lion Fight shows no active 2026 dates (the promotion's listed activity ends in 2023), and ONE Championship had no US card surfacing. Nothing from Kings Combat or Church Street Boxing could be checked before the budget ran out.

Still open and worth a second pass next week: (1) the opponent and time for the Knicks home game Ticketmaster lists on Nov 27, plus any Celtics/Pacers/Nets home dates before Dec 6, and any proper Brooklyn watch-party bar; (2) Kings Combat's own event calendar and any Williamsburg gym showcase; (3) Church Street Boxing's fight-night schedule, relevant because it is next to where he teaches in Tribeca; (4) ticket on-sale status and price tiers for UFC 334; (5) whether any boxing promoter has a Theater at MSG or Sony Hall date in November; (6) England's November international window and a Brooklyn soccer bar showing it. None of these could be confirmed, so none are listed as candidates rather than guessed at.
